Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

FOOTBALLS. VOLLEYBALLS, BASKETBALLS, NETBALLS, 

THROWBALLS AND WATER-POLO BALLS 

PART 2 VOLLEYBALLS 

( Fourth Revision } 



1. Scope — Covers requirements for volleyballs excluding tlie bladder. 

2. Shape, Dimensions and Mass 

2.1 When inflated to an air pressure of 040 to 045 bar {0-40 to 0*45 kgf/cm^). the ball shall be 
spherical in shape with a circumference of 65 to 67 cm. 

2.1.1 A tolerance of 1 percent in the circumference on sphericity shall be allowed. 

2.2 Mass of the ball with inflated bladder shall be 260 to 280 g. 

3. Materials 

3.1 Z.eaf/?er — The balls shall be manufactured from butt portion of tight textured cowhide or 
buffalohide, free from flay cuts and grain defects, vegetable/semi-chrome or chrome tanned, dyed in 
any colour or pigmented as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. At the end of tanning 
operation, and before drying, suitable fungicides shall be incorporated for all types of leather. 
Fungicides used to promote resistance to mould growth in the leather shall be effective and 
non-toxic and their optimum dosage shall be pre-determined (see LB : 3 of IS : 6191-1971 Methods of 
microbiological colour fastness and microscopical tests for leather). The material shall show no 
growth of mildew when examined visually after completion of the test in accordance with LB : 2 of 
IS ; 6191-1971. The tanned leather shall be substantially fat-liquered or oiled or both and the surface 
obtained shall be smooth and well set. The leather panels of the volleyballs shall have a minimum 
thickness of 15 mm and minimum tensile strength 19 6C0 kN/m* ( approx 200 kgf/cm^ ) with 
maximum 55 percent elongation at break when measured on any four panels diametrically opposite 
to each other, in addition, average thickness of leather panels shall not be less than 17 mm when 
measured on any four panels of the volleyballs. 

3,1.1 For testing the tensile strength and temporary elongation, the test methods covered in 
IS : 5914-1970 'Methods of physical testing of leather', shall be followed. The double hole stitch 
strength shall be minimum 60 kgf/cm thickness of leather when tested according to LP : 8 of 
IS : 5914-1970. 

3.2 Tiiread for Stitciilng 



3.2.1 /./nen fftread — Rot-proofed and having 4 plies shall be used for stitching. The minimunrr 
breaking strength of single yarn shall be 45 kgf when tested by the method given in IS : 1670-1970 
'Method for determination of breaking load, elongation at break and tenacity of yarns ( first revision )\ 

3.2.2 Cotton //?reatf — Conforming to variety No. 34 of 13:1720-1978 'Specification for cotton 
sewing threads ( second revision )\ 

3.3 Lining Ciotii — Sub\ecX to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier, volleyball covers 
may be provided with new cotton long-cloth or poplin lining. 

3.4 Coiour — Subject to the requirements of purchaser, preferably uniform light colour. 

4. Construction and Workmanship 

4.1 The balls shall be made from a suitable number of panels of shapes capable of giving sphericity. 



(§ 4.2 Stitctiing — The ball shall be stitched with linen or cotton thread and shall have 24 ± 2 stitches 
per decimetre. The stitches shall be well stretched. When the ball is inflated to the air pressure given 
in 2.1, the visible threads shall not be more than 2 mm deep from the surface of the ball. The panels 

to for volleyballs should preferably be cut with self-cutting-cum-perforating dies.

4.3 Mouth — The mouth shall be adequate and permit the nozzle of the inflating pump or needle to be 
accommodated and suitable means shall be provided to deflate the ball. The neck of the bladder shall 
be completely inside the mouth. 

5. SampMfig and CriterUi for Conformity — Shall be as agreed to between ttie purchaser and the 
supplier. The recommended scheme for the same is given in 5.1. 

5.1 Lot — In any consignment, all the baJIs manufactured from the same raw material under slmi(«r 
conditions shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

5.1-1 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the standard samples of balls 
shail be collected and tested separately for each lot. 

5.1.2 Number of bails selected at random from the lot depends upon the size of the lot and shall be 
in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. 

TABLE 1 SAMPLE SIZE AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

5.1.2.1 The number of balls in a sample shall be selected at random from the lot and in order to 
ensure the randomness of selection, IS : 4905-1968 'Methods for random sampling' may be followed. 

5.1.3 Number of tests and criteria for conformity — Each ball in the sample shall be inspected for 
shape, dimensions and mass according to 2; materials according to 3 and construction and workmanship 
according to 4. A ball failing in any one or more of these requirements shall be considered as 
defective. The lot shail be considered as conforming to these requirements if the number of 
defecthre balls in the sample does not exceed the number given in col 3 of Table 1. 

6. MarWng — Unless otherwise required by the purchaser, each ball shall bear the manufacturer's 
name, initials or trade-mark. 

6.1 ISJ Certification MarA/n^ — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — Each ball shall first be wrapped in a polyethylene cover and then packed together with 
other balls similarly wrapped according to the instructions of the purchaser. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

The third revision of this standard was issued in 1974. On the suggestion of the Consultative 
Committee of Parliament for the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports, the standard in this revision 
has been brought in line with the international rules of the game. The alterations made in this revision 
include modifications in the values of air pressure and in sampling clauses and specification of 
references to the relevant Indian Standards for methods of test for various characteristics of leather.
